pack.title: BuzzOff Pick & Mix
pack.description: A full show of general knowledge with a European accent: ten board categories, a Football category for Final Trivia and five Fast Money surveys. Distances are in kilometres. Survey numbers are illustrative, not from a real poll.
pack.author: BuzzOff

categories.title: Names the Same
categories.blurb: Two people, one first name. Tell us the name they share.

clues.question: What first name is shared by the footballer Messi and the singer Richie?
What first name does the "Twilight" actor Lautner share with his wife, who is also a Lautner?
clues.notes: Taylor Lautner married Taylor Dome in 2022 and she took his surname.

clues.question: What first name connects the actors Rogen and Green?
What first name connects the actress Adams and the singer Winehouse?
What first name connects the "Star Wars" creator Lucas and the Manchester United legend Best?

categories.title: Exploring Bodies
categories.blurb: Human anatomy, from the bones outwards.

clues.question: Which bone is the longest and largest in the human body?
What is the largest organ of the human body?
Which organ stores bile and releases it to help with digestion?
clues.notes: The liver makes bile; the gallbladder only stores and releases it.

clues.question: Which part of the brain handles higher-level processes such as reasoning, memory and sensory information?
clues.notes: "Cerebrum" is close but is the larger structure; the cortex is its outer layer. Host's call.

clues.question: Which body system controls the production and regulation of hormones?

categories.title: Tip2Tip
categories.blurb: Estimate a distance in kilometres. Each clue says how close you need to be.

clues.question: To the nearest 500 kilometres, how far is it in a straight line from London to Rome?
clues.notes: About 1,430 km as the crow flies, which rounds to 1,500.

clues.question: To the nearest 500 kilometres, how far does China extend from north to south?
clues.notes: Roughly 5,500 km from north to south and 5,200 km from east to west.

clues.question: To the nearest 10 kilometres, how wide is the English Channel at its narrowest point?
clues.notes: The Strait of Dover is about 33 km across, from the South Foreland near Dover to Cap Gris-Nez near Calais. Give 40 at your discretion.

clues.question: To the nearest 1,000 kilometres, how far does Russia extend from east to west?
clues.notes: About 9,000 km, across eleven time zones.

clues.question: To the nearest 1,000 kilometres, what is the distance over the Earth's surface from the North Pole to the South Pole?
clues.notes: Half of the Earth's circumference through the poles. The metre was first defined so that the distance from the pole to the equator came to 10,000 km.

categories.title: Few-Wheeled Vehicles
categories.blurb: Things you ride or drive on three wheels or fewer.

clues.question: Which single-wheeled vehicle is associated with circus performers and acrobats?
Which famous Italian scooter brand made its debut in 1946?
clues.notes: Made by Piaggio. "Vespa" is Italian for wasp.

clues.question: Which three-wheeled motorised taxi is a common sight in Southeast Asia?
Which self-balancing, two-wheeled personal transporter was invented by Dean Kamen?
Which three-wheeled Italian delivery van, built by Piaggio since 1948, takes its name from the Italian word for bee?
clues.notes: Said "AH-peh".

categories.title: PlayStation Legends
categories.blurb: Heroes from three decades of Sony's consoles.

clues.question: Which orange marsupial, PlayStation's unofficial mascot in the 1990s, spins through crates and collects Wumpa fruit?
Which wisecracking treasure hunter is the hero of the "Uncharted" series?
Which Spartan warrior, known as the Ghost of Sparta, is the hero of the "God of War" series?
Which flame-haired hunter takes on robot dinosaurs with a bow in "Horizon Zero Dawn"?
clues.notes: Said "AY-loy".

clues.question: In the "Ratchet & Clank" series, Clank is a robot. What species is Ratchet?

categories.title: Not an Alloy
categories.blurb: Every answer is a metal, and a pure one.

clues.question: Which abundant metal is commonly found in kitchen utensils and kitchen foil?
Which shiny precious metal is traditionally used for fine tableware?
Which metal is a liquid at ordinary room temperature?
Which metal in a cheap gold-coloured ring can turn the skin underneath it green?
Which highly corrosion-resistant metal of the platinum group has been called the most valuable precious metal?
clues.notes: Its price swings wildly, so "most valuable" is true in some years and not in others.

categories.title: Douze Points
categories.blurb: The Eurovision Song Contest, from 1956 to today.

clues.question: At the Eurovision Song Contest, what is the highest score a national jury can give to a single song?
Which Italian rock band won Eurovision in 2021 with "Zitti e buoni"?
clues.notes: Said "MOH-neh-skin". It is Danish for moonlight.

clues.question: Which Finnish heavy-metal band won Eurovision in 2006, dressed as monsters, with "Hard Rock Hallelujah"?
Which Canadian singer won Eurovision for Switzerland in 1988?
clues.notes: With "Ne partez pas sans moi", by a single point.

clues.question: In which Swiss city was the very first Eurovision Song Contest held, in 1956?
clues.notes: Seven countries took part and the hosts won, with Lys Assia.

categories.title: Real Creamers
categories.blurb: Milk, cream and the things made from them.

clues.question: What do you get by churning cream?
Which Italian word names a denser, slower-churned style of ice cream?
Which sugar found in milk is digested with the help of the enzyme lactase?
Which heat treatment makes raw milk safer to drink by reducing harmful microorganisms?
clues.notes: Named after Louis Pasteur.

clues.question: Which French blue cheese, made from sheep's milk, must be matured in the natural caves of Mont Combalou?
clues.notes: The caves lie under the village of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon in the Aveyron.

categories.title: Hypothetically Speaking
categories.blurb: Every answer is a theory or a theorem.

clues.question: Which theorem relates the sides of a right-angled triangle with the formula a² + b² = c²?
Which scientific theory explains how the Earth's continents sit on huge slabs of crust that slowly move?
clues.notes: Continental drift was Alfred Wegener's earlier idea; plate tectonics is the theory that explained it.

clues.question: Which cosmological theory describes the universe expanding from an early hot, dense state?
Which theory developed by Albert Einstein changed our understanding of space, time and gravity?
clues.notes: "Special relativity" alone leaves out gravity. Host's call.

clues.question: Which field of mathematics studies strategic decisions made by rational participants?

categories.title: Boggle
categories.blurb: Find the word. Answers grow by two letters a clue: 2, 4, 6, 8, then 10.

clues.question: Give a two-letter word meaning to move or travel.
Give a four-letter word for something uninteresting or lacking excitement.
clues.notes: The intended answer is DULL. Other four-letter words that fit are the host's call.

clues.question: Which six-letter word means a financial plan of expected income and spending?
Which eight-letter word means exaggerated or assertive masculine pride?
Which ten-letter word names a decorative light fitting that hangs from the ceiling?

categories.title: Football
categories.blurb: The European game. Pick it for Final Trivia and the last clue is asked.

clues.question: Which two Spanish clubs meet in the match known as El Clásico?
clues.notes: Both are needed.

clues.question: Which Argentine scored the "Hand of God" goal against England at the 1986 World Cup?
Which country shocked the continent by winning Euro 2004, beating the hosts Portugal in the final?
clues.notes: 1–0, with a header from Angelos Charisteas.

clues.question: Which English club went the whole 2003–04 Premier League season unbeaten and became known as "the Invincibles"?
In the 2005 Champions League final in Istanbul, which club led Liverpool 3–0 at half-time and still lost?
clues.notes: Liverpool scored three in six minutes and won on penalties. Inter is not correct.

surveys.question: Name a flavour of ice cream.
What percentage would you tip for good service?
How many times a day do you go to the toilet?
Name something a person might get caught in.
Name something a doctor might remove from somebody.
